title: Signed evaluation compatibility of a normalized scalar comparison
statement: Let $X,R,S,\alpha,p,L,K,l,k,B$ have the meanings of [def-pur-ordinary-line-scalar-data], with $L,K$ locally free of rank one. Let $b:L\otimes_R S\cong K$ and require the signed family $B$ to satisfy the tensor-power and dual normalizations of [lem-pur-signed-line-scalar-tensor-tower]. Suppose ordinary natural isomorphisms $o_m$ have the forward balanced formula $s\otimes(x\otimes y)\mapsto(s\otimes x)\otimes B_m(1\otimes y)$. Suppose derived natural isomorphisms $d_m:D_pF_{L,m}\cong F_{K,m}D_p$ satisfy the fixed representative square on every flat-term K-flat complex. Then, for every $Y\in D(R)$ and integer $m$, the composite of $d_{-m}(F_{L,m}Y)$, $F_{K,-m}(d_m(Y))$ and the fixed target evaluation $\epsilon_{K,m}(D_pY)$ equals $D_p(\epsilon_{L,m}(Y))$. The evaluations are the actual normalized evaluations of the given line data; the statement asserts their compatibility for an already constructed comparison, not the existence of a comparison.

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat representative of Y. Tensor by each signed power and scalar extension preserve such models. Substitute the two supplied representative equations and the two line evaluation computation equations.

The resulting ordinary cochain square can be checked on sheafified generators. Both paths send ((x tensor y) tensor z) tensor s to x tensor s alpha(ev(y,z)): the signed-power comparison preserves the actual evaluation, and commutativity identifies the two scalar orders. The signed basis normalization uniquely identifies the line-data evaluation with this contraction. This includes m=0 and negative m. Explicit local check: on a slice trivializing L, transport a basis through b to K. The recorded signed bases e_n and f_n satisfy B_n(1 tensor e_n)=f_n by hB. Both normalized evaluations take the opposite basis pair to 1. On a e_m tensor c e_{-m} their values are ac and alpha(a)alpha(c), respectively. Bilinearity and sheaf separatedness extend equality from these local bases to arbitrary sections, including zero and negative exponents.
Apply localization to the ordinary cochain square. Naturality along the chosen representative isomorphism gives the desired square on Y, so it is independent of the representative.
